title: Thermite-foil flash anneal: reactive Al/Ni layers crystallize BaTiO3 in-cell
idea: Borrow the reactive multilayer foils used for soldering: cap the capacitor stack with a 20 nm Al/Ni nanolaminate and ignite it with a pulse. The self-propagating reaction delivers a ~1 ns, >1000 C local heat spike that crystallizes the BaTiO3/SrTiO3 dielectric into high-k perovskite while the transistors below stay under 400 C.
why: Fact 1: crystalline perovskite at k ~200+ becomes BEOL-compatible without a high-thermal-budget anneal, and the NiAl product becomes the top electrode. Only Al, Ni, Ba, Sr, Ti and O.

title: Morphological-box test chip: 10,000 storage-element combinations per wafer
idea: Box = {all six axes varied on purpose}: a standard periphery wafer carries 10,000 1-kbit tiles, and gradient sputtering, area-selective ALD and maskless e-beam give each tile its own medium, electrode, access device and anneal. On-chip BIST logs retention tails, endurance and disturb automatically, so the morphological box becomes a physical experiment that outputs a ranked Pareto map of combinations every month.
why: Cuts the learning cycle for new storage elements by ~100x and finds non-obvious medium/electrode pairs that single-material programs miss.

title: Eliminate static storage: recirculating magnon delay-line loops hold bits in flight
idea: Eliminate the stationary storage element: bits circulate as spin-wave packets (wavelength ~50-100 nm) in 100-um closed YIG or CoFeB waveguide rings, with one magnetoelectric transducer per ring that regenerates and taps the stream. A ring holds ~1-2 kbit with ~50 ns average latency; storage is travel time, not a held state.
why: Removes capacitor, retention and refresh (facts 1, 3) because regeneration is part of circulation; no per-bit lithographic cell, only a waveguide ring; density today ~10x below DRAM, so the target is streaming KV/activation buffers at aJ-per-bit hold energy.

title: Midpoint-bootstrapped stacked switch nulls storage-node leakage
idea: MINIFY the voltage across the leakage path to millivolts: the write switch is split into two series transistors and their midpoint is driven by a small feedback transistor from the read device that mirrors the stored level, so the inner switch sees ~0 V drain-source during hold (a sample-and-hold trick applied per cell).
why: Leakage 100-1000x lower so retention reaches seconds (fact 3) in any foundry node; a 4T cell designable by a small team.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall bit in ScAlN or lithium niobate nanomesa
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: in each single-crystal nanomesa, a ns voltage pulse creates or erases a charged domain wall that conducts ~10^4x better than the bulk; the bit is wall present/absent, read non-destructively by a small current. Switching is ferroelectric with no ion motion, and CMOS-friendly wurtzite ScAlN is the target host.
why: Fact 8: non-destructive read with no restore; fact 3: nonvolatile, no refresh; crosspoint 4F2 with one lithography level.

title: Repurpose LTPS display backplanes as giant 1T1C memory sheets
idea: Worsen: make memory only on 300 mm silicon at ~$10/cm2. Flip: an AMOLED backplane is already a 1T1C array, so re-mask an existing LTPS display line (3 um cells, storage caps, access TFTs) into memory sheets; $1M buys a re-spun driver IC and a 24-month cost-per-bit study for cold bulk-capacity tiers.
why: Capital and cost per area (~100x cheaper per cm2) using idle display-fab capacity; 100 ns-1 us latency fits a capacity tier.

title: Si: anodized mesoporous-silicon storage node multiplies capacitor area
idea: Electrochemically anodize a 1-2 um silicon layer under the array into 5-10 nm mesopores, then ALD-coat TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each storage node is a sponge instead of one etched pillar; a 30x30 nm footprint captures ~10-30 pores and ~20-50x its planar area.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): reaches 5+ fF without a 60-75:1 plasma etch, removing the hardest etch/deposition steps; per-cell pore-count variation is the main risk.

title: Open printed-memory PDK and ink library for distributed iteration
idea: IFR: thousands of labs test a new storage element every week at near-zero cost. Closest achievable: publish an open R2R process kit (standard printed electrode and access layers, test-structure layouts, characterization scripts) plus a shared ink bank so any lab can drop a new storage ink into a known stack.
why: Speeds discovery and grows the U.S. talent base; cost per experiment drops from ~$100k fab shuttle to ~$100 print run.

title: Solar-cell field-effect passivation shell around the storage junction
idea: Adapt PERC/TOPCon solar passivation: wrap storage-node junction sidewalls in ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm-2 fixed negative charge, and replace the implanted node contact with a 1.2 nm tunnel-oxide/poly-Si passivating contact, removing implant damage and repelling carriers from interface traps.
why: Fact 3: the leakage tail comes from a few trap-rich junctions; solar data show ~10x lower surface recombination, aiming at 3-10x longer tail retention and proportionally fewer refreshes.

title: MLCC-style interdigitated nanolaminate capacitor at cell scale
idea: Scale down the multilayer ceramic capacitor from mm to nm: conformally deposit 4-6 alternating electrode/dielectric layers in each hole, with odd and even electrodes tied at opposite ends, so capacitance multiplies by layer count instead of by aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall: ~3x Cs at the same AR, or a 25:1 AR cell matching today's Cs.

title: Fire-stick land manager: Ge-doped VO2 hysteresis latch, laser processed
idea: Aboriginal fire-stick land management uses controlled heat, not irrigation. A Ge-doped VO2 nanobridge (transition near 90 C) is biased inside its insulator-metal hysteresis window, where it holds a 0 or 1 phase on nW of standby power. Pulsed-laser shock cleaning and laser annealing replace wet cleans and furnaces.
why: ~1 ns, low-voltage switching (fact 10) in a compact two-terminal cell (fact 4). Laser processing makes the storage module dry, a more than 10x water cut.

title: CBRAM's hot-retention killer fixed by intermetallic-compound filaments
idea: Adesto/Crossbar Ag and Cu filaments dissolved at 125 C because a few-atom metallic chain has high surface energy and diffuses away. Switch in an amorphous Ge-Te or Si-Te matrix where injected Cu reacts into a Cu2Te or Cu3Ge compound filament, a thermodynamic minimum rather than a metastable chain, and reset it by field-driven decomposition.
why: Moves CBRAM retention from ~85 C to Grade 1 while keeping ns low-voltage writes in a dense crosspoint.

title: Atanasoff capacitor drum as transistorless capacitors swept by MEMS brushes
idea: The 1942 ABC stored bits on capacitors mounted on a rotating drum, read and regenerated by brushes, with no switch per capacitor. Fabricate a field of isolated nano-capacitors (10-nm dielectric, no junction, no transistor) under a 2D MEMS array of conductive probe tips, each tip scanning a 50x50 um field with its own sense amp.
why: Without an access transistor leakage is dielectric tunneling only, so retention goes from 64 ms to hours (Fact 3 refresh ~0); ~2F2 cells with no wordline; microsecond 'drum tier' that needs a DRAM cache.

title: Hin-invertase dipole rotor: molecular rotor crystal flips orientation
idea: Bacteria toggle genes when Hin invertase flips the orientation of a DNA segment, and the inversion persists through division. Use an amphidynamic crystal of dipolar molecular rotors (fluorinated phenylene rotors in rigid stators) with the rotation barrier engineered to ~1 eV. A gate field turns the dipoles 180 degrees in ns, and their collective dipole shifts an FeFET-like channel threshold.
why: Non-volatile ferroelectric-like bit from rotation inside a rigid framework, so there is no oxygen-vacancy fatigue or wake-up as in HZO. Deposited at low temperature from solution or vapor.

title: Ba: BaTiO3 negative-capacitance layer boosts series storage capacitance
idea: Stack a thin BaTiO3 ferroelectric in series with the cell's linear ZrO2 and tune thicknesses so the ferroelectric runs on its stabilized negative-capacitance branch; the series stack then exceeds the linear capacitor alone, giving more charge per area at the same voltage.
why: Raises Cs at fixed AR (fact 1) or keeps charge at lower voltage (fact 10); Ba and Ti are abundant; whether quasi-static negative capacitance is stable and hysteresis-free is contested.

title: Vacuum-gap floating electrode written by Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, oxide-free
idea: For reactor and deep-space users whose oxides trap radiation charge and wear out, the storage node is a metal island over a sealed 2-3 nm vacuum gap; electrons are written and erased by field emission through vacuum and the island gates a read transistor. Vacuum has no bonds to break or traps to fill, so tunnel wear disappears.
why: A flash-like non-volatile, non-destructive-read cell with DRAM-class endurance: no refresh (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1), ~10-100 ns writes at 3-5 V; gap uniformity at the angstrom level is the risk.

title: Electrolytic capacitor trick: anodized porous niobium with self-healing oxide
idea: Electrolytic capacitors win with porous foil plus an anodic oxide that regrows over any defect; sputter Nb through a self-ordered porous-alumina template to form nanorod electrodes, grow the Nb2O5 dielectric (k~40) by room-temperature anodization (~2.5 nm/V, self-limiting), and periodically 're-form' arrays with a slight over-bias that heals leakage sites.
why: Facts 1 and 3: litho-free high-area electrodes and a self-limiting, self-healing high-k dielectric made in a beaker instead of ALD, attacking cost and the leakage tail; Nb comes from Brazil/Canada, avoiding tantalum sourcing; needs only sputter, anodization bath and furnace.

title: Snap-through buckled nanoribbon holds bits as geometry
idea: MINIFY a MEMS bistable beam to a 10 nm x 80 nm pre-stressed SiC or amorphous-carbon ribbon arched up or down; GHz-range resonance allows ~1 ns electrostatic snap-through writes, and position is read through the gap-capacitance change to an under-electrode.
why: Zero leakage, zero refresh, no capacitor wall (facts 1, 3); flip energy ~aJ; fatigue life of the ribbon is the open question.

title: Antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bit written by spin-orbit torque
idea: Combine the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn with a BiSb topological-insulator spin-orbit-torque write line and a tunnel-magnetoresistance read: the antiferromagnetic order switches in picoseconds, produces no stray field so cells pack at pitch without crosstalk, and ignores external fields. The order is stable at zero power.
why: Zero refresh, dense packing with no stray-field spacing, ps switching and effectively unlimited endurance; small read signal is the risk; avoids W and Pt write lines.

title: Eliminate net magnetization: antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bits read by anomalous Hall
idea: Eliminate the ferromagnet, the fixed layer and the MgO tunnel barrier: store the bit in the octupole order of the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal underlayer in ~100 ps, and read it from its large anomalous Hall voltage in a simple Hall cross. With no stray field, cells pack at ~10 nm pitch without coupling.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free (fact 3), immune to charge-coupling disturb (fact 9); the stack shrinks from ~15 sputtered layers to ~2, cutting tool time; risk is the uV-scale Hall signal needing local gain.

title: Field-immune antiferromagnetic Neel-vector bit for EMP-hardened military memory
idea: EMP-hardened systems need storage unaffected by external fields, so the bit is the Neel vector of a noncollinear antiferromagnet such as Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque in ~10-100 ps and read through its anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance. Zero stray field lets cells pack at minimum pitch without dipolar crosstalk.
why: Unlimited endurance, non-volatile, picosecond writes potentially below DRAM CV2 energy (fact 10); removes refresh entirely; small readout signal is the main risk.

title: Antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bit flipped by spin-orbit torque
idea: IFR: a bit with no stray field, no wear and picosecond speed. Closest achievable: a noncollinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn) whose magnetic octupole order is switched by spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal line and read via its large anomalous Hall or tunnelling signal; zero stray field lets cells pack at minimum pitch.
why: Nonvolatile and wear-free, so no refresh (fact 3) and immune to charge-coupled row hammer (fact 9); density gain from zero dipolar crosstalk.

title: Nanosecond protonic three-terminal bit with non-destructive channel read
idea: Worsen: use two-terminal cells where read and write fight over one path. Flip: store the bit as proton concentration in a 10 nm WO3 channel, moved through a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte by ~5 ns gate pulses and read by channel conductance on a separate path at <0.1 V.
why: Non-volatile, non-destructive read (facts 3, 8) and sub-volt reads (fact 10); hydrogen is not a scarce resource.

title: Zn: MgZnO/ZnO quantum-well charge bucket under a sense channel
idea: Deposit a ZnO quantum well clad by Mg0.3Zn0.7O barriers (conduction-band offset ~0.4-0.6 eV) beneath a thin oxide read channel; electrons parked in the well screen the channel and shift its threshold, so retention comes from a band offset rather than a thick capacitor dielectric.
why: Replaces the capacitor (facts 1, 2) with a low-temperature, BEOL-stackable heterostructure of abundant Zn and Mg for many 3D tiers; defect-assisted leakage out of the well is the risk.

title: Printed conducting-polymer ion-doping bit read as channel conductance
idea: IFR: a transistor whose channel is itself the memory. Closest achievable: an organic electrochemical transistor (PEDOT:PSS class) where a pulse pushes ions into or out of the printed channel and a barrier layer pins them; read current is nondestructive and multilevel.
why: Fact 8 and cost: nondestructive read on printed foil; small devices have reached sub-us switching, and 100 nm scaling targets tens of ns.

title: Weathervane: surface-anchored dipolar molecular rotors with nitrile dipoles
idea: Stimulus 'weathervane' (points one way until pushed) -> a monolayer of tripod-anchored molecular rotors whose paddle carries a strong nitrile/nitro dipole (not the usual fluorinated dipole groups), designed with two detents 180 degrees apart; a gate field flips the paddles and the collective dipole shifts a FET threshold by ~0.3 V.
why: Molecular-scale (~1 nm^2) nonvolatile bit with nondestructive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1), deposited from solution at room temperature (fact 4).

title: Paper-mill layered magnet: gated vdW ferromagnet spin-filter tunnel bit
idea: Like pressing paper sheets, stack a few layers of the room-temperature vdW ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2 with hBN. A gate pulse switches interlayer coupling between ferro and antiferro alignment, and spin-filter tunneling changes the current by >100x.
why: Fact 10: a magnetic bit set by voltage, not current, at aJ energy. The giant read signal allows small sense amps (fact 7), and it is nonvolatile, so no refresh.

title: Magnetoelectric exchange-coupled write: attojoule polarization flips magnet
idea: Put a 20 nm La-doped BiFeO3 layer under a CoFe nanomagnet: a ~100-200 mV pulse rotates BFO's coupled ferroelectric/antiferromagnetic order, and interfacial exchange drags the magnet 180 degrees. An MTJ on top reads the state.
why: Write energy is ~2Pr*A*V ~ 1e-16 J for a 30 nm cell at 0.1 V, ~1000x below current-driven STT and well under the CV2 floor of fact 10.

title: Swap smooth electrode for dealloyed nanoporous metal sponge electrode
idea: Deposit an AlTi or AgAu alloy as the storage-node electrode and selectively dissolve the less noble element, leaving a nanoporous sponge with 5-10 nm ligaments and 10-30x the surface area. ALD then coats the dielectric and top electrode conformally.
why: 10x or more effective area per footprint breaks the charge wall (fact 1) with a short, relaxed-pitch DUV cap and no high-AR etch or EUV (fact 4).

title: Polarization-division multiplexing: charge plus polarization in one node
idea: Like fiber links sending two polarizations on one fiber, store two orthogonal variables per node: a low-field charge level and the polarization direction of a thin ferroelectric layer in the same stack, read first by low-field charge sensing, then by high-field switching-current sensing.
why: 10x at same cost: 2 bits per node x 5 vertical tiers, with both variables sharing one capacitor and one access device.

title: Rotate the array into depth: four capacitors stacked in one trench
idea: Rearrange the 2D array vertically: in a 1990s-style 0.25 um wide, 10 um deep trench, deposit alternating doped-poly electrodes and collar oxides to form four isolated storage capacitors stacked along the trench, each reached by its own buried strap and sidewall transistor at a different depth (depth-addressed wordlines).
why: Density without a litho shrink (fact 4): four cells per trench footprint, ~25 fF each (2 um2 of 5 nm ONO per segment); risk is forming straps and transistors at depth.

title: Moire superlattice traps self-assemble a ten-nanometer bit lattice
idea: Invert 'cells must be lithographically patterned' -> let a twist angle draw them. A twisted hBN/WSe2 stack on glass forms a moire potential with ~10 nm period, each minimum a trap holding a few electrons; relaxed-pitch crossbar gates address blocks and an adjacent 2D charge sensor reads occupancy.
why: Lithography-free ~1e12 sites/cm^2 (density, EUV elimination, fact 4); room-temperature retention needs >100 meV moire depth and single-site addressing is unsolved.

title: Thousand-composition sputter library hunts for k-over-100 dielectrics
idea: MAGNIFY experiment throughput ~1000x: co-sputter three targets with deliberate thickness gradients onto one 150-mm wafer pre-patterned with 1,000 MIM test capacitors, then auto-probe k, leakage at 1 V and breakdown overnight, screening ternary oxide spaces such as Ti-Zr-La-O weekly.
why: A fast, cheap route to k >= 70 at <= 1e-7 A/cm2 (fact 1) without big-fab capital.

title: Rank-order charge encoding survives common-mode leakage drift
idea: Invert 'each cell's charge level carries data absolutely' -> encode data in the relative order of charges in a group. Four cells written to four distinct analog levels encode one of 24 permutations (4.58 bits per 4 cells); because leakage drags all levels down together, the rank order survives long after fixed thresholds fail, and a read is a local comparator sort.
why: Stretches refresh interval ~4-10x (fact 3) and adds ~15% bits per cell (cost/bit); tail cells that break order are handled by a light outer code.

title: Molecular spin-state bit: hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover film
idea: Instead of moving electrons in and out of a node, flip their pairing inside an ion: a thin film of a room-temperature-hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover complex toggles between low-spin and high-spin with ~10-20% dielectric-constant change; a field/charge pulse sets the state and a capacitive divider reads it.
why: Refresh (fact 3): a bistable molecular state needs no refresh and molecule-scale units (~2 nm) promise density; risks are solid-film switching speed and cycling.

title: Chameleon: spin-crossover molecules toggle high-spin and low-spin states
idea: Stimulus 'chameleon' (changes color on cue) -> a 10 nm film of an Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover complex with room-temperature thermal hysteresis; a local ns heat or field pulse switches molecules between low-spin and high-spin, changing film permittivity and conductance by ~10-30%, read by a thin-film transistor gated through the film.
why: Intrinsically bistable molecular bit (no refresh, fact 3), solution-processed with no EUV (fact 4), built from earth-abundant iron.

title: Cold-chain DRAM: 77 K operation shrinks storage node height
idea: Borrow LNG/cryogenic logistics: run DRAM in liquid-nitrogen immersion, where leakage falls ~1e6x, then redesign the storage node to ~0.5 fF (a short AR ~8 cup) because retention becomes minutes.
why: Facts 1, 3 and 4: deletes the HAR capacitor module and refresh; cryocooling is amortized at datacenter scale.

title: Dual-mode HZO capacitor snapshots to polarization on self-refresh entry
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): power states are only those DDR defines. Run an HZO capacitor below its coercive field as a plain DRAM capacitor in normal operation; on Self-Refresh Entry the die sweeps rows above coercive field to store data as polarization and powers the array off, and after Self-Refresh Exit each row's first ACT performs the destructive ferroelectric read and restores it as charge within tRCD.
why: Self-refresh power falls to ~0 (fact 3: refresh is 16-33% of idle power) while ferroelectric switching happens only per power-down, so ~1e11 FE endurance is ample; lazy restore fits within tXS.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bits: polarization set by atomic-layer registry
idea: Flip the direction of motion: in bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2, sliding one layer in-plane by one bond length reverses the out-of-plane polarization (AB to BA stacking); write with a vertical field pulse, read by tunnel-current asymmetry, with no ion displacement or oxygen vacancies to fatigue.
why: Endurance and density: sliding ferroelectrics switch essentially fatigue-free in 0.6 nm films, enabling nonvolatile no-refresh cells stacked by layer transfer; risk is wafer-scale stacking-order control.

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor channel that stores and reads its own bit
idea: Use alpha-In2Se3, whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization sets its own band bending and conductance, as the transistor channel. A gate pulse writes the polarization, and the read is a non-destructive channel conductance with no separate capacitor or ferroelectric gate stack.
why: Storage and gain merge in one 2D layer, removing the capacitor (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8). Enables a vertical 4F2 cell with no capacitor etch.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer stacking registry as the bit
idea: IFR: switch the bit by nudging atoms, not by pushing charge across barriers. Closest achievable: in rhombohedral bilayer hBN or MoS2 the AB vs BA stacking registry carries opposite out-of-plane polarization; a ~0.3 V pulse slides one layer by one bond length and the polarization is read as a threshold shift in an adjacent 2D channel.
why: Facts 1 and 10: no capacitor, sub-volt write (CV^2 down ~10x), atomically thin so tiers stack for 3D (fact 2); sliding has a tiny barrier and reported fatigue-free switching.

title: Printed alpha-indium-selenide ferroelectric semiconductor flake ink
idea: IFR: a channel that remembers by itself with no separate dielectric. Closest achievable: inkjet exfoliated alpha-In2Se3 nanoflakes, a 2D ferroelectric semiconductor whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization modulates its own conductance, so each printed flake is a two-terminal or FET bit.
why: No capacitor (fact 1), low-temperature printing, sub-volt switching; no oxygen-vacancy wake-up as in oxide ferroelectrics.

title: Magnetosome biomineralization: protein-templated nanomagnet arrays without magnetic etch
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria grow uniform single-domain magnetite crystals using Mms6/MamC proteins. Anchor engineered Mms6 peptides in pre-patterned wells on a tungsten- and platinum-free spin-orbit write line (e.g. BiSb topological insulator), so each well grows one uniform 15-20 nm ferrite particle from aqueous solution. A tunnel-barrier read stack is capped on after growth.
why: Non-volatile. Removes ion-beam etching of MTJ stacks (MRAM's yield and capex bottleneck), narrows the switching distribution through uniform particle size, and runs as an aqueous room-temperature process.

title: Fermented magnetosome bits: bacteria grow uniform magnetite memory crystals
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria grow 35 nm single-domain Fe3O4 crystals with <10% size spread, uniformity that sputter-and-etch cannot match. The crystals are harvested, given DNA linkers and docked into lithographic sites on Pt or W spin-orbit-torque lines. Each bit is held as magnetization and read through magnetite's half-metallic tunneling.
why: Spin storage with unlimited endurance and no MTJ etch damage. The fab tool is a fermenter, which cuts capital intensity, and pitch is ~50 nm for nonvolatile working memory.

title: Cryogenic quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 capacitor at 77 K
idea: Combine liquid-nitrogen-cooled memory pools with SrTiO3 or KTaO3, quantum paraelectrics whose permittivity climbs from ~300 at room temperature to over 1000 near 77 K. A 5 nm STO film in a planar or AR-10 capacitor then delivers 5 fF without high-AR pillars.
why: Fact 1 and capital: k rises 15-50x over ZrO2, so the capacitor module drops from 60:1 etch to near-planar (~50% lower capacitor-module capex); thin-film k is below bulk, which is the risk.

title: Sand-mandala monk: dry-sprayed BaTiO3 nanocrystal planar capacitor
idea: A monk builds a mandala grain by grain without water. Aerosol deposition fires sub-micron BaTiO3 particles at the wafer at room temperature, where they fracture and bond into a dense ceramic film (k in the hundreds) with no sintering, solvent or rinse; the film serves as a planar high-k storage capacitor.
why: With k in the hundreds, a planar capacitor holds enough charge without the 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1), which deletes the high-AR etch and its many cleans. The dry, room-temperature spray uses more than 10x less water.

title: Gate voltage flips interlayer magnetic order in a 2D magnet
idea: Effect walk: electrostatic doping-tuned interlayer exchange. In bilayer CrI3-class or room-temperature Fe3GaTe2 van der Waals magnets, a ~0.1 V/nm gate field shifts interlayer exchange between antiparallel and parallel, switching a spin-filter tunnel junction resistance by >10x with a purely capacitive write.
why: No current flows through the junction during write (~aJ at sub-volt) and spin-filter read has very large TMR, so access energy can be 10-100x below DRAM; Curie temperature and air stability are the risks.

title: Logic-fab BEOL finger capacitors as DRAM storage nodes
idea: Combine the metal-oxide-metal finger capacitors that every logic back-end already offers with BEOL oxide-semiconductor access transistors, so a standard logic interconnect stack (interdigitated M3-M8 lines) becomes the storage capacitor field. No special capacitor module, high-AR etch or memory fab is needed: any U.S. logic fab can print DRAM-class memory above its own logic.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: uses existing domestic back-end tooling with zero new capex; density is ~1/3 of commodity DRAM but the memory sits on-die (fact 5).

title: Defect charge-state memory in silicon carbide color centers
idea: Combine quantum-sensing color centers with memory: divacancies in 4H-SiC switch between stable charge states when an electrical pulse injects carriers in a p-i-n structure, and the charge state persists for hours to years in the dark. Read is electrical, through the defect ensemble's effect on junction capacitance, at ns speed.
why: Zero refresh, radiation hard, on a material with U.S. production (SiC power wafers); signal per cell and density are speculative.

title: Conveyor-belt CCD loops: charge packets recirculate, no capacitor per bit
idea: Treat memory as an assembly line. Bits are charge packets clocked around closed buried-channel CCD rings of 64-256 wells, and each ring has a single sense/regenerate station, so every lap is a refresh. No bit has its own access transistor or capacitor, only overlapping gates.
why: Facts 1, 3 and 7: the capacitor and access-transistor leakage are gone. A bit costs ~4F2 of gate and the periphery is shared across a whole ring. Fits streamed pages such as KV cache, with <=64 ns rotation latency.

title: Lung-surfactant monolayer prevents high-AR pillar collapse during drying
idea: Lung surfactant lowers its surface tension as an alveolus shrinks, so small alveoli do not collapse. Before the final rinse-dry, coat storage-node pillars with a fluorinated phospholipid-like monolayer whose surface tension falls on compression. The capillary forces that pull AR >100 pillars together (stiction) then self-cancel as the gap narrows.
why: Charge wall via yield (facts 1, 4): makes AR 100-150 pillars survivable in wet processing without supercritical dryers or extra support meshes, for ~1.5-2x Cs.

title: Significance-aware HBM lanes: compact cells for bf16 mantissa bits
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): DQ lanes and bursts stay identical. Because inference stacks lay out bf16/fp8 tensors with fixed bit positions per DQ lane, build core dies whose arrays behind sign/exponent lanes keep full-size capacitors while arrays behind low-mantissa lanes use half-height capacitors with relaxed retention (raw BER ~1e-4), enabled by an existing mode-register write and defaulting to full reliability.
why: ~25-35% less capacitor height/area per stack for AI inference where LSB errors are tolerable (density, cost per bit) with an identical interface; depends on controller address and lane mapping.

title: Po: memory that tops itself up — plate-pumped self-restoring cell
idea: Po: the memory refreshes itself. Extracted: add a two-terminal threshold switch and a diode in series between each storage node and the plate line; a global low-amplitude AC carrier on the plate tops up only nodes already above threshold (stored 1s) while 0s stay below it, making 1T1C self-restoring without extra transistors.
why: Removes row-by-row refresh commands and their bandwidth/power cost (fact 3). Per-cell threshold variability is the risk.

title: Electrostatic pull-in hysteresis latch held at zero static current
idea: A sputtered TiAl nanobeam over a dielectric-capped electrode is bistable at any hold voltage between its release and pull-in voltages. A small up or down pulse sets the state, the capacitive hold draws no DC current, and the read senses the ~2x capacitance change; process is <=400 C BEOL MEMS.
why: Static storage held by electrostatics, with no leakage-driven refresh (fact 3), no capacitor charge requirement (fact 1) and no ohmic contact to wear. Dielectric charging and stiction are the risks.

title: Park VO2 inside its hysteresis loop; nudge bits with heat or strain
idea: Effect walk: thermal hysteresis of the VO2 metal-insulator transition. A strain- and dopant-engineered VO2 array (Tc ~90 C, ~15 K loop) is held at a regulated mid-loop temperature so metal and insulator are both stable; a 1-ns Joule nudge of a few kelvin writes 'metal', a piezo strain pulse that lifts the loop writes 'insulator', and the ~10^3 resistance ratio is read at 50 mV.
why: Write only supplies the latent heat of a ~10-nm volume (~0.2 fJ) plus a strain nudge, and read uses tiny bias on huge contrast: ~10x below DRAM cell+bitline energy with zero refresh, using the chip's waste heat to hold state.

title: Optane's 85 C ceiling raised by a tensile cage around amorphous GST
idea: Optane-class PCM was rated for only ~85 C retention because amorphous GST crystallizes when hot. The amorphous phase is ~6-8% less dense than the crystal, so wrap each cell in a pre-stressed SiN/TiN liner that holds its volume in tension; tension penalizes the denser crystal and should raise the effective crystallization barrier by ~0.2-0.4 eV.
why: Pushes 10-year retention past 125 C without Ge-rich alloys that slow writes, keeping ~100 ns PCM speed for automotive and industrial memory.

title: Triboelectric generators: contact-electrified charge patches store bits
idea: Triboelectric nanogenerators move a saturating charge between dissimilar surfaces on contact; let an e-beam-defined, electrostatically actuated Ti cantilever tap a PTFE- or Al2O3-coated pad above a sensing transistor, transferring a self-limiting ~50-500 e- charge per contact, and reverse it by tapping with an opposite-polarity material, the patch retaining charge with electret-grade stability.
why: Electret retention (years) removes refresh, and the self-limiting transfer tolerates actuator variation; buildable with e-beam, sputter and sacrificial release; small charge per contact, wear and ns actuation are the risks.

title: Dual-mode cell parks its charge in a trap layer
idea: Jump timescales inside one cell: in active mode the bit lives on the capacitor (ns access); before idle or power-down, a high-voltage pulse pushes the state into an adjacent charge-trap nitride (years retention), and on wake it is restored to the capacitor.
why: Refresh power: idle refresh (16-33% of idle power) disappears; also gives instant-on persistence.

title: Relaxor polar-nanoregion dielectric for k near 70
idea: Scale down to 2-5 nm polar nanoregions: dope ZrO2/HfO2 laminates with La/Nb to make a relaxor-like dielectric whose nanoregions rotate freely under field (slim loop, no remanence), giving high effective permittivity without ferroelectric hysteresis loss.
why: Capacitor wall: Fact 1 says k~70 is the escape; relaxor behavior targets k 50-80 at 5 nm thickness, about 2x charge at today's AR.

title: Williams-tube logic: a flat-panel display fab used as a memory fab
idea: The Williams tube turned a display into memory; do the same with existing Gen-8.5 IGZO TFT display fabs, where every pixel is already a 1T1C charge cell. Pattern dense 1.5-um-rule TFT memory arrays (no liquid crystal, no light) on glass, tile them with TFT sense amps, and cut them into memory sheets.
why: Glass avoids CZ silicon and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles; ~66 kb/mm2 x 5.5 m2 is ~45 GB per sheet at roughly $10/GB on idle display capacity, parity in a shortage; us-class latency means a CXL capacity tier.

title: Vacuum nanochannel field-emission valve as cell access device
idea: Fuse vacuum-tube electronics with the DRAM cell: each storage node reaches the bitline through a sealed 10-20 nm vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip and a collector, gated by a ring electrode. Below the field-emission threshold no carrier exists in the gap, so the node cannot leak; raising the gate field emits electrons for ns-speed write and read.
why: Fact 3: refresh eliminated; the vacuum gap is temperature-insensitive, so hot (125 C) operation carries no retention penalty, and it is radiation hard.

title: Thermos-style sealed vacuum isolation around each storage node
idea: Borrow vacuum-flask insulation: replace STI oxide next to each storage node with sealed vacuum cavities (sacrificial carbon ashed out, then capped by non-conformal deposition), so no oxide traps or bulk paths remain between adjacent nodes.
why: Facts 3 and 9: removes trap-assisted leakage and the electron-migration path behind row hammer; aims at ~10x higher hammer threshold and lower node-to-node coupling.

title: Thermos flask: vacuum-isolated node behind a zero-leakage nanorelay
idea: Stimulus 'thermos' (vacuum stops heat leaking) -> replace the access transistor with an electrostatic nanorelay whose contact opens a 5 nm vacuum gap, and wrap the storage node in a sealed vacuum cavity, so the off path has no semiconductor junction or channel to leak through. Stored charge decays only by field emission across the gap, negligible at 1 V.
why: Kills the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3): retention moves from 64 ms to minutes, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss >100x; relay pitch is not bound by transistor EUV layers (fact 4).

title: Snap-through buckled nanobeam: contactless mechanical bistable bit
idea: Box = {medium: up or down buckled shape of a pre-compressed 120 nm SiN/Si nanobeam | access: row/column electrostatic electrodes, no transistor | sense: capacitive gap readout through a shared column amplifier | integration: sealed vacuum-cavity array in BEOL | substrate: Si | fab: sacrificial-oxide release + ALD seal}. Built-in compressive stress pushes the beam past Euler buckling so it has two stable shapes; a 1-2 V pulse snaps it through in ~1 ns (GHz resonance), and it never touches a surface, so there is no stiction or contact wear.
why: Facts 3 and 10: zero leakage and zero refresh, elastic switching energy ~1 fJ, endurance limited only by elastic fatigue; removes the access-transistor leakage tail entirely.

title: Po: the transistor is empty — vacuum-channel access switch per cell
idea: Po: the transistor is empty. Extracted: isolate each storage node with a sealed ~5 nm vacuum nano-gap field-emission switch; below the Fowler-Nordheim threshold the gap has no carriers at all, so off-current falls exponentially below the 13 fA tail, and a gate-assisted emission pulse opens it for read/write.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): retention from 64 ms to minutes or hours, removing most of the 16-33% idle refresh power and 10-20% bandwidth loss. Emission voltage and emitter stability are the risks.

title: Bead-strung vortex cores: nanoring magnets threaded on vertical wires
idea: Revive hand-strung core memory: deposit ~40 nm permalloy nanorings as 'beads' around vertical metal pillar 'strings'. Pillar current writes clockwise or counterclockwise vortex chirality by Oersted field, and the flux-closed rings have no stray field, so 4-8 can stack on one pillar and be read through a ring-segment MTJ.
why: Fact 2: multi-bit vertical stacking on a single pillar with no per-bit transistor. Zero stray field packs bits densely, with unlimited endurance.

title: Gunn-domain delay line: travelling field domains as a shift register
idea: 1960s engineers proposed Gunn-effect domains as high-speed memories. Launch bits as high-field domains travelling ~1e5 m/s along a long n-GaN or GaAs channel, recirculate them through a regenerating trigger electrode, and tap them with capacitive pickups along the channel.
why: ~1-um bit spacing at 100 Gb/s per channel and ~10 ns per mm tap latency with no cell structure at all; domain stability at sub-um scale is very uncertain.

title: Colloidal-sphere inverse-opal electrode gives area without a high-aspect etch
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality + #31 Porous materials: self-assemble 5-8-nm silica nanospheres in each shallow cell well, ALD-coat TiN/ZrO2/TiN through the interstices, then dissolve the spheres to leave a 3D inverse-opal capacitor whose curved shells multiply area ~6-10x per volume at AR <10:1.
why: Facts 1 and 4: replaces the 60-75:1 pillar etch and its tool capital with a self-assembled scaffold, giving the same Cs in a squat cell.

title: Ca: polycrystalline Ca3Ti2O7 hybrid-improper ferroelectric, grain spread tolerated
idea: Sputter Ca3Ti2O7, whose polarization arises from coupled octahedral rotations (low coercive field, no Pb, Hf or Zr), as a polycrystalline capacitor film; random grain orientation widens the Pr spread, and cells with too few aligned grains (~1%) are corrected by the code instead of demanding epitaxy.
why: Non-volatile 1T1C with no pillar (fact 1), all abundant elements and a low-temperature, non-epitaxial process (fact 4); film behaviour below 20 nm is unproven.

title: N: silicon-nitride nanostring parametron stores bit as oscillation phase
idea: Pump GHz Si3N4/AlN nanomechanical resonators (Q~300) at twice resonance so each settles in ~100 ns into one of two oscillation phases, 0 or pi, as in Goto's 1950s parametron; one frequency comb pumps thousands of resonators, and phase slips up to ~1% per hold interval are corrected by the code.
why: Dynamical bistability needs no stored charge, so there is no leakage tail (fact 3) and no capacitor (fact 1); pump power is the cost.

title: Sputtered complementary-oxide SRAM layer stacked over any chip
idea: MINIFY the fab to a sputter tool: room-temperature sputtered p-type SnO and n-type ZnSnO thin-film transistors form cross-coupled 6T latches above finished foundry CMOS; repeat the 4-mask module to stack several memory layers.
why: Static, refresh-free memory in monolithic 3D without EUV (facts 2, 4), all-U.S. tools; p-oxide mobility limits access to ~10-50 ns.

title: Proton-transfer organic ferroelectric (croconic acid) as low-voltage polar bit
idea: Box = {medium: polarization from collective proton hopping along hydrogen bonds in croconic acid | access: Si FET | sense: FeFET threshold shift | integration: vapor-deposited BEOL layer | substrate: Si | fab: low-temperature thermal evaporation}. Switching moves only protons by ~1 angstrom inside hydrogen bonds, with no heavy-ion motion, which gives coercive fields far below hafnia and lets the layer be deposited below 150 C over finished logic.
why: Voltage floor (Fact 10) and BEOL stacking: sub-1 V nonvolatile switching, and the tiny thermal budget lets many tiers stack.

title: Si/SiGe superlattice selectively oxidized into 100-plate stacked capacitor
idea: Combine GAA nanosheet epitaxy with selective conversion: grow 100 alternating Si/SiGe layers, cut a slit, replace the SiGe with high-k through Ge-selective etch and ALD refill, and silicide alternate Si sheets contacted from two opposite staircases to form an interdigitated stack. Horizontal plates become stacked storage capacitors for 3D DRAM tiers with no vertical high-AR hole.
why: Facts 1 and 2: capacitance grows with tier count instead of AR, and one epi stack serves both transistor and capacitor tiers, aiming at the 26+ tier break-even.

title: Po: memory that forgets on purpose — millisecond selector-capacitor crosspoint
idea: Po: memory that forgets on purpose. Extracted: drop the transistor and accept ~1-10 ms retention: a steep two-terminal tunnel selector in series with a planar MIM capacitor at every crossing of DUV-patterned lines, 32 layers deep at 2 bits per cell, refreshed by a background engine that sweeps an entire layer in parallel.
why: 4F2 x 32 layers x 2 bits with no EUV and no transistors gives roughly 100x more bits per wafer dollar than 6F2 1T1C. Trade-offs: high refresh energy and selector leakage, offset by parallel layer-wide refresh.

title: Swap tall pillar for on-chip multilayer-ceramic nanolaminate capacitor
idea: Deposit ~100 alternating ALD layers of TiN (3 nm) and ZrO2 (4 nm) and cut each cell block with one DUV etch. Then recess and insulate the odd electrodes on one sidewall and the even ones on the other (like MLCC end terminations), so all plates connect in parallel.
why: ~100 stacked parallel plates give pillar-class Cs (fact 1) from a ~0.7 um low-AR block at DUV pitch, with no EUV and no 60:1 etch (fact 4).

title: Swap big capacitor for small charge plus electron-multiplying readout
idea: Store only ~500 electrons on a shallow capacitor at DUV pitch. At read, the packet passes through a short EMCCD-style impact-ionization gain register on the bitline (gain ~20-100) before the sense amplifier.
why: Needs ~10x less Cs (fact 1), so planar or AR <8:1 caps work without EUV or a high-AR etch (fact 4); EMCCD gain registers already reach sub-electron noise.

title: SiGe quantum-well hole pocket extends floating-body retention
idea: Scarcity rule: silicon-family materials only, no capacitor. Grow a buried Si0.6Ge0.4 well in the body of a vertical gate-all-around channel; its ~200 meV valence-band offset traps holes written by impact ionization or GIDL and shifts threshold for read, while the offset blocks hole recombination into source and drain.
why: Capacitorless 4F2 vertical cell (facts 1, 2, 4) with ~100x longer retention than plain floating-body cells via band confinement; SiGe epitaxy is mature in U.S. fabs.

title: Charge-density-wave domain switching in 1T-TaS2 picosecond bit
idea: MAGNIFY speed and MINIFY energy: a 10-nm 1T-TaS2 film is switched by a ~30 ps electrical pulse into a metastable hidden charge-density-wave domain state (~1000x resistance change) and erased by a longer pulse; run in a ~200 K module where the metastable state lasts seconds to hours, giving refresh-light dynamic memory.
why: ~fJ writes, ps speed, non-destructive resistive read (fact 8) and no atomic motion so endurance may be unlimited.

title: Po: the bit is a traffic jam — charge-density-wave domain switching
idea: Po: the bit is a traffic jam of electrons. Extracted: thin 1T-TaS2 (or strain-stabilised variants) switches between commensurate and nearly-commensurate charge-density-wave states with ps electrical pulses; the bit is which electronic crystal is frozen in, read as a ~10x resistance difference.
why: Ps-scale, aJ writes with no capacitor at all (facts 1, 10). Room-temperature retention and BEOL integration of layered sulfides are open questions.

title: Nested charge-trap shadow layer preserves data through heal cycles
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: embed a ~2-nm SiN charge-trap layer inside each capacitor dielectric so that before a repair anneal, detox or module removal the controller programs a nonvolatile shadow copy of every bit with a Fowler-Nordheim burst, then restores it afterwards. Repairs no longer need external data migration, and the shadow is used rarely so its endurance suffices.
why: Repairability: makes in-place healing practical on full arrays; also gives power-loss persistence for free.

title: Gated lateral thyristor latch in thin SOI foundry
idea: MINIFY the bistable to one gated PNPN body: in a 45/22 nm SOI MPW, a lateral thyristor with a capacitively coupled gate holds '1' by regenerative latching and '0' by blocking, with ~nA holding current and ~1-2 ns gate-pulse writes; no capacitor, no refresh.
why: Static cell at ~8-12F2, about 5x denser than SRAM (fact 3 avoided); standby current is the trade.

title: Metastable DX-centre traps with lattice-relaxation recapture barriers
idea: Worsen: trap charge behind thin barriers that tunneling defeats. Flip: store charge in an engineered layer of DX-like centres (Si-doped AlGaN or Ga2O3 defect complexes) whose large lattice relaxation creates a configurational barrier to recapture, giving persistent stored charge for hours at room temperature, written and erased by gate pulses.
why: Retention orders of magnitude beyond the 13 fA tail (fact 3) without a big capacitor (fact 1).

title: Low-barrier volatile MTJ refreshed by the REF commands DDR already sends
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): DDR insists on refresh, so make refresh useful. Use a 12-15 nm STT-MTJ designed with low thermal stability (Delta ~25-30, retention of seconds), which cuts write current ~4x so a tiny access transistor suffices, and let standard REF commands trigger internal read-and-rewrite of aging rows; holding costs zero leakage.
why: MRAM-style 1T1R density with DRAM refresh semantics, ~50 fJ writes and no capacitor (facts 1, 2); low current density extends barrier life, but retention spread and write-error rate are risks.

title: Anodized aluminum nanopore capacitors replace plasma-etched silicon pillars
idea: Invert 'HAR capacitors must be plasma-etched into a silicon wafer' -> let electrochemistry grow them on aluminum. Anodizing an aluminum plate self-organizes hexagonal pores (~40-60 nm pitch, AR 100+) in minutes; ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines each pore as a cup capacitor, the aluminum is the common plate and heat spreader, and oxide-TFT access and wiring are built on the planarized top.
why: Delivers AR >100, past fact 1's AR-115 regime, with no HAR plasma etch, no EUV and no quartz-crucible silicon, cutting capacitor-module capex >10x; pore-to-TFT registration is handled by pre-patterned anodization seeds or several pores per cell.

title: 1960s holographic memory revived on thin-film lithium niobate photonics
idea: RCA and Bell holographic stores wrote whole pages as interference gratings in photorefractive crystals. Put an Fe-doped thin-film LN slab under a SiN optical phased array that steers the reference angle electro-optically in ns, storing ~1000 angle-multiplexed 4-kb pages in a 100x100 um slab read in parallel onto a Ge photodiode row.
why: Volume storage escapes planar litho density (Fact 4) and a page read uses the overfetch instead of wasting it for streamed weights (Fact 8); thermal fixing for retention; target 10 Gb/cm2 equivalent with no transistor per bit.

title: Refrigerator crisper drawer: thermoelectrically chilled cell array only
idea: Keep only the drawer cold, not the kitchen: integrate a thin-film SiGe or Bi2Te3 thermoelectric layer under the cell-array mats only, holding storage nodes ~25-30 K below the periphery and logic, with heat pumped into the package lid. Junction leakage roughly halves every ~8-10 K.
why: Fact 3: a 25 K drop cuts leakage ~6-8x, stretching refresh from 32 ms to ~200 ms; net gain requires array idle power share >20% and thermoelectric COP >~0.5 at small dT; SiGe avoids tellurium supply risk.

title: S: CaS:Eu,Sm electron-trapping film read by on-chip light
idea: Coat each cell with ~50 nm of CaS:Eu,Sm electron-trapping phosphor; a blue micro-LED or electrical injection pushes electrons into Sm traps (write), and an infrared pulse releases them as Eu emission detected by an under-cell photodiode (destructive read, as in DRAM).
why: Deep (~1 eV) traps give long retention with no capacitor (fact 1) and no access-leakage path (fact 3); Ca and S are abundant and the rare earths are trace dopants; on-chip optical I/O speed is the hurdle.

title: Mn: Mn4N ferrimagnetic racetrack shifts domain-wall bits at km/s
idea: Build racetracks from Mn4N (only Mn and N, perpendicular anisotropy, near-compensated so walls move ~1-3 km/s) and shift domain-wall-encoded bits past one read/write port with current pulses, so tens of bits share a single access transistor.
why: Amortizes access transistors and periphery (fact 7) over many bits with no capacitor (fact 1) for a large density gain; free of rare earths and cobalt; shift reliability is the risk.

title: Cloud DFT screen for a k-70 dielectric that ALD can grow
idea: Worsen: keep the k ~40 ZrO2 stack forever. Flip: spend ~$300k of cloud compute on a high-throughput DFT and phonon screen of rutile and alloyed oxides (Ti-Ge-Sn-O, Hf-Ti-O) for k >= 70 with band gap >= 4 eV and ALD growth below 450 C, then test the top five in a university ALD within 24 months.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): k 70 lets AR fall from 75:1 to ~45:1, a cheap route to a step change.

title: Eliminate storage-node lithography: transistors electroplate their own capacitor towers
idea: Eliminate the storage-node mask and etch: after building the access transistors, immerse the wafer in a plating bath and turn on every wordline so each working transistor's drain contact sources current and plates its own Ni/Ru nanotower; then add ALD dielectric (N2 purge) and top plate. No argon-sputtered seed is needed because the drains are the seeds.
why: Self-aligned capacitor with no litho layer and no etch (fact 4); towers reach AR 100+ by plating time (fact 1); dead transistors grow no node, giving a built-in yield screen; risk is plating uniformity across billions of sites.

title: Nitrogen-immersed DDR5 DIMMs with sub-femtofarad cryo-optimized cells
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): same DDR5 edge connector and protocol, so move the whole DIMM into the LN2 or cold-plate loop of an AI rack. At 77 K access leakage falls >1e6, so a redesigned array uses ~1 fF planar capacitors with half-length bitlines to keep Cs/Cbl and holds data for hours, while the PHY is retuned for 77 K thresholds but signals per spec.
why: Removes the HAR capacitor (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3), and higher mobility allows lower voltages (fact 10); nitrogen is abundant (no helium), cooling energy is the tradeoff.

title: Eliminate the oxide capacitor: band-offset germanium quantum-well hole pocket
idea: Eliminate the external capacitor: grow a 5-nm SiGe or Ge quantum well beneath a vertical Si access channel so its ~300-500 meV valence-band offset traps holes as the stored bit, shifting the channel threshold; a heterobarrier rather than a junction sets retention, 10-100x longer than plain floating-body cells.
why: Capacitor-less ~4F2 cell with retention near the 64 ms spec (facts 1, 3), epitaxial with no HAR capacitor etch; risk is band-to-band generation in Ge.

title: Honeycomb: anodized alumina pores template 500:1 capacitors, no plasma
idea: Stimulus 'honeycomb' -> anodize an aluminum film in oxalic acid so it self-organizes into hexagonal pores (40-60 nm pitch, AR up to 500:1), guided by a nanoimprinted pre-dent, then ALD TiN (from TiCl4/NH3) and ZrO2/Al2O3 into the pores. The electrolyte digs the holes: no fluorocarbon etch, no NF3 chamber clean.
why: Breaks the 60-75:1 AR wall toward >115:1 (fact 1) and removes the capacitor-hole EUV/etch step (fact 4); ~2x Cs or half the footprint, fluorine-free.

title: Parametron revived: AlN nanoresonator phase bits made in U.S. filter fabs
idea: Box = {medium: 0 or pi oscillation phase of a parametrically pumped 2-5 GHz AlN nanoresonator | access: frequency-multiplexed pump rows, no transistor | sense: phase-sensitive mixer per column | integration: resonator arrays released over CMOS | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: the AlN BAW/FBAR filter lines already running in Colorado and Texas}. Goto's 1954 parametron stored bits as subharmonic phase; at Q~1e4 and aJ stored energy the pump dissipates ~0.1 pW per bit, and a write injects a seed tone during pump ramp-up.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no leakage and no capacitor, static energy comparable to DRAM refresh, built with domestic MEMS capacity instead of DRAM fabs.

title: A battery per bit: LiPON nano-cell stores the bit as voltage
idea: Swap stored charge for stored chemistry: each 180 nm-patterned cell is a ~50 nm-thick LiCoO2/LiPON/Si thin-film battery (LiPON: Oak Ridge, 1992) whose state of charge is the bit, read non-destructively as open-circuit voltage by a high-impedance FET; self-discharge, not junction leakage, sets retention.
why: Refresh and destructive read (facts 3,8): months of retention, no charge sharing, multilevel via voltage plateaus; risks are Li diffusion speed for ~100 ns writes and intercalation endurance.

title: CaMKII avalanche chain: small trigger magnet flips a stable cluster
idea: CaMKII holoenzyme subunits phosphorylate their neighbours, so one activated subunit switches the whole ring and keeps it switched. Make each bit a chain of 6-12 exchange-coupled nanomagnets. A short SOT pulse switches only the low-barrier 'trigger' magnet at the end, and the reversal runs down the chain as a domain wall; the chain's collective barrier (>60 kT) sets retention.
why: Decouples write current from retention: write energy is set by the small trigger (~5-10x lower), while retention scales with chain size. Non-volatile, with MRAM-like unlimited endurance.
